note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, conditions, and quotes; both correctly bind the display-size, safety, and dinner-party requirements to the right entities. Each set states the TV and computer display sizes twice (once in inches, once in centimeters), so both carry the same redundancy. A labels the metric values with the vaguer attribute 'minimum size' while B keeps one consistent attribute name, but neither is misread or invented. No claim in either set is wrong against the page text.
remarks: Both sets omit several facts on the page: the common food-allergies list (k.vii), the 'refrigerate after opening' storage example (k.vi), the guest-decathlete point-deduction rules (d and j.i), the eligible/ingredient file reference (g), that the computer may be a laptop or desktop, that there is no required volume setting, and the observer spot-check procedure (9-4.b). The display-size duplication (in. and cm as separate claims) is a recurring pattern in both extractions; unit conversions of the same requirement should be merged into one claim.
